case_id_note: case_id is a convenience label added for this worked example, NOT a native AGF field. The real correlation chain is reconstructed from the reference fields inside each artifact below (see narrative.md, section 'Correlation: real FK vs reconstructed').

delegation_chain._depth_validation_note: Spec 02 §3.6/§6: max_depth is a static ceiling checked as len(chain)-1 <= min(max_depth across all tokens). This chain has 3 tokens → len-1=2 → all tokens require max_depth >= 2. Values (3,2,2) satisfy this bound; hop1's attenuation is carried by scope/constraints, not by reducing max_depth.

hop0_root_mandate._kind: delegation JWT payload (decoded; Spec 02 authority object) — unsigned in this synthetic trace

hop1_A_to_B._kind: delegation JWT payload (decoded) — attenuation: scope narrowed from 3 actions to 1

hop2_B_to_C._kind: delegation JWT payload (decoded) — attenuation: same action, added value/target constraints

revocation_record._kind: kernel invalidation.schema.json shape (Spec 05 branch-cut / Spec 28 propagation)
revocation_record.subject: del_hop1_c204be
revocation_record.deployment_topology_note: This scenario's revocation_effective_at→revocation_observed_at gap models a file/cached-revocation-list-backed deployment only. Under a live-Postgres-backed deployment (postgres / postgres+notify), detected_at is written in the same transaction as revoked_at and this gap would be zero — see Spec 28 §4.3.
revocation_record._actor_authorization_note: Provenance only: the specs (Spec 02, Spec 05 §4.3, Spec 00 §3.6) require an actor/revoked_by DID but do not currently define who is authorized to revoke a given authority. This is a genuine spec gap, not something this trace resolves. A draft RFC (0000-revocation-authorization, agf-standards/rfcs/) proposes a grantor-or-ancestor rule for this — status Draft, not adopted, so it does not currently govern whether `did:agf:acme:alice` (root grantor, not del_hop1_c204be's direct issuer) was authorized to revoke del_hop1_c204be here; under that RFC's own proposed rule, alice would qualify as an ancestor. A candidate agf-runtime enforcement of that proposed rule exists (RR-0002, agf-profile/implementation/review-records/ — status Pending) but implements a runtime-specific actor-to-delegation binding the RFC deliberately leaves unresolved at the spec level, so it is cited here as an existing implementation data point, not as evidence the spec question is settled.

_kernel_field_mapping.note: Existing field names are kept here for readability; this maps them to invalidation.schema.json's native field names.

evidence.reason: vendor payment authority narrowed after incident review; del_hop1_c204be revoked directly. Under branch-cut semantics (Spec 05 §3), del_hop2_9e5b71 is invalidated as a descendant even though it is not itself named as a revocation subject.

revocation_record.note_on_issued_vs_effective: AGF's branch-cut model treats a revocation as effective at the instant it is recorded (Spec 28 §4.3, single-instance deployment — no propagation delay to the index). issued_at and effective_at are therefore the same instant here; the real gap in this deployment model is issued/effective vs. observed (i.e. occurred_at vs. detected_at in the kernel schema), not issued vs. effective.
revocation_record.note_on_detected_at_persistence: detected_at is a real, persisted field in the reference runtime for every revocation backend. For live-Postgres-backed deployments (postgres / postgres+notify), detected_at is written in the same transaction as revoked_at — there is no lag, ever, by architecture. The 32-second revocation_effective_at-to-revocation_observed_at gap this trace depicts is only realistic for a file/cached-revocation-list-backed deployment, which is the topology this scenario should be read as modeling. This does not change the separate, still-true finding that AGF performs exactly one authority check per decision with no re-validation at the instant of execution — detected_at is about when a revocation was first observed, not about re-checking authority at execution time.

decision_receipt._kind: kernel decision.schema.json shape — signature omitted (synthetic trace)

action.request_ref_note: Correlation identifier only; does not provide cryptographic evidence binding.
action.request_hash_note: SHA-256 hex digest over this worked example's own canonical JSON encoding of {action_target, amount, from_account, scope, to_account} — keys sorted, no whitespace; see narrative.md 'Payload identity' section for the exact canonical byte string and how to recompute it. This is this worked example's own illustrative convention for demonstrating what payload-identity binding across decision/execution/settlement would look like. AGF does not currently specify a canonical request/payload hashing method, field set, or canonicalization rule — compare policy.hash below, which has the same illustrative-only status. The same value is carried on execution_receipt, settlement_record, and reconciliation_exception below; a mismatch there would mean the records describe different payloads, which is the property this field exists to let a reviewer check — something request_ref alone cannot do.

policy.note: hash and constraint evaluation (e.g. max_amount) are illustrative-only, not tied to a specified evaluator or hash algorithm.

decision_receipt.note: Correct decision at decided_at: the revocation had not yet been issued (revocation_issued_at=1785852001 > decided_at=1785852000). This is not a stale-cache bug — the chain was genuinely valid at evaluation time.

wire_spec07_unsigned.note: Defined by Spec 07 §10.1 but explicitly outside the signed payload per §10.2 — operational detail, never invalidates a receipt.

org_id.note: Spec 07 §5.3 defines org_id only as a Decision storage-path segment, not a field on the execution_receipt wire object.

execution_receipt.request_ref_note: Correlation identifier only; does not provide cryptographic evidence binding.
execution_receipt.request_hash_note: Same value and convention as decision_receipt.action.request_hash — matching here is what establishes this receipt describes the same payload the decision authorized, not just a shared correlation string.
execution_receipt.dispatch_log_ref_note: No gateway dispatch log supplied in this synthetic trace; execution_attempted_at is asserted, not log-evidenced, here.
execution_receipt.signature: <omitted — synthetic trace, no real ES256 signature>
execution_receipt.upstream_event_ref_note: Synthetic correlation only, this worked example's own convention — not an AGF or Spec 07 field. Ties this receipt's upstream_status to settlement_record.states[0] (the 'accepted' entry) as the same upstream acceptance event, since nothing native links execution acceptance to settlement acceptance otherwise.
execution_receipt.propagation_window_clarification: Spec 05 §5.5 governs a new decision evaluation during/after the propagation window; this scenario models the dispatch of an already-issued decision without a second authority evaluation. This is a scenario about the gap between decision-time and execution-time authority, not a claim that AGF permits dispatch after revocation.
execution_receipt.propagation_window_runtime_evidence: The 'no second authority evaluation between decision and dispatch' claim above is verified against the current agf-runtime reference implementation, not merely asserted: perform_decision() (src/presentation/api/routes/decide.py:115) is called exactly once per request by /v1/decide (decide.py:996) and by each of the three gateway-proxy routes (http_gateway_proxy.py:141, mcp_gateway_proxy.py:123, a2a_gateway_proxy.py:151) — no second or independent revalidation call exists anywhere in that codebase as of this note. This is cited as reference-implementation behavior, not as normative specification text: no AGF spec currently states single-check decision semantics as a requirement (a draft RFC, 0000-single-check-decision-semantics, proposes formalizing this — status Draft, not adopted). Two implementations could in principle diverge on this point while both remaining silent-conformant.
execution_receipt.execution_time_validation_status: Spec 30 (Execution-Time Authorization Validation, RFC 0000-execution-time-authorization-validation) defines a gate that closes exactly this window — see the sibling execution_validation_check block below for what it produces for this scenario. As of RR-0003 (agf-profile/implementation/review-records/, Approved 2026-08-15), this gate is now agf-runtime's shipped default (settings.execution_time_validation_enabled = True) for the built-in HTTP/MCP/A2A gateway proxies. The outcome recorded on this execution_receipt (dispatch proceeded, outcome: executed) reflects this trace's original, pre-RR-0003 point-in-time capture — preserved as the historical account of the gap Spec 30 was built to close, not a claim about current default behavior. A fresh occurrence of this exact scenario against a current, default-configured deployment would instead follow execution_validation_check's outcome: blocked before dispatch.
execution_receipt.note: execution_attempted_at is a gateway-local dispatch timestamp, not a field on the signed kernel receipt itself (the kernel schema only signs completed_at, i.e. when the outcome was known). Flagging this because it matters for the proof/inference matrix: the moment of dispatch is evidenced by infra logs, not by the cryptographically signed artifact.

execution_validation_check._kind: Spec 30 §4 Execution Validation Record shape — NOT part of this trace's original point-in-time execution_receipt above, which was captured before RR-0003 (Approved 2026-08-15) made this gate agf-runtime's shipped default. This block models what the check produces for this exact chain/timeline with the gate on — as of RR-0003, this is the actual current default behavior for a fresh occurrence of this scenario, not a hypothetical.
execution_validation_check.invalidation_refs_note: References revocation_record.subject. Spec 30 §4 has invalidation_refs point at the revoking backend's own invalidation-record id when one exists (PgRevocationStore rows have one); this synthetic trace's revocation_record has no such id minted, so — matching Spec 30 §4's documented fallback for backends without a distinct id (e.g. FileRevocationStore) — it falls back to the jti of the revoked authority itself.
execution_validation_check.checked_at_vs_dispatch: checked_at (1785852002) is the same instant as execution_receipt.execution_attempted_at — the gate runs immediately before dispatch, per Spec 30 §3, not at some other point in the timeline.
execution_validation_check.outcome_if_enabled: Dispatch at 1785852002 would have been blocked (HTTP 403 / JSON-RPC -32000, AGF_EXECUTION_VALIDATION_INVALID per Spec 30 §5's error shape) instead of proceeding to execution_receipt.upstream_status: accepted. execution_receipt.outcome would read not_executed, not executed, and settlement_record / reconciliation_exception below would not exist for this request at all — reconciliation would have nothing to find, because there would be nothing to reconcile.

settlement_record._kind: synthetic — not an AGF-native concept; AGF has no payment-rail model. Rail-neutral account push, 3-state (accepted/settled/reconciled) settlement model.
settlement_record.request_ref_note: Correlation identifier only; does not provide cryptographic evidence binding.
settlement_record.request_hash_note: Same value and convention as decision_receipt.action.request_hash — the amount/from_account/to_account/target fields below are exactly what that hash was computed over, so this record's payload identity is independently checkable against the decision, not merely asserted by re-listing the same numbers.
settlement_record.beneficiary_note: Beneficiary identity is out of scope for this example and is not distinguished from to_account; AGF has no native beneficiary concept.
settlement_record.upstream_event_ref_note: Synthetic correlation only — see execution_receipt.upstream_event_ref_note. Ties states[0] below to the execution receipt's upstream_status as the same upstream acceptance event.

reconciliation_exception._kind: synthetic — post-execution reconciliation job cross-checking settled payments against the revocation index
reconciliation_exception.revoked_authority_ref_note: Points at the revoked authority's jti; revocation_record has no id field of its own to reference instead.
reconciliation_exception.request_hash_note: Same value and convention as decision_receipt.action.request_hash — carried here so the reconciliation job's cross-check is itself checkable against the same payload identity, not just against the chain of *_ref pointers.
reconciliation_exception.scope_note: Intentionally terminal at exception-opening; SLA/ownership/closure lifecycle is out of scope — this scenario is about the revocation race window, not reconciliation process design.
